tagline: A slow loop through the Port City and around the lake.
intro: The loop sets out from the Isabel Holmes Bridge over the Cape Fear River and works south through downtown Wilmington on the street grid the city finalized in 1743. Water Street follows the river beside the Riverwalk, a promenade of about a mile and three quarters. South Front Street holds some of the city's most exclusive homes, and Castle Street and South Fifth, once home to the seaport's workers, make up the heart of the historic district.
Fifth Street leads out to Greenfield Park and around the lake on Lake Shore Drive, and the loop comes back up Third Street past the government buildings and old churches.

moments.title: 1898 Memorial Park
moments.text: The park marks November 10, 1898, when white supremacists overthrew the city's elected biracial government, with deaths estimated from 60 to more than 300.

moments.title: Battleship North Carolina
moments.text: Across from the Riverwalk lies the battleship North Carolina, which got away from its tugs on the way in, in 1961, and ran into a floating seafood restaurant.

moments.title: Greenfield Park
moments.text: Lake Shore Drive takes a long turn around Lake Greenfield and past what the state guidebook calls the world's largest Rotary Club International sign.
